transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm a barber, and I'm here because... I've basically gotten to the point where I will do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work. I'll try to switch clients with someone else, or tell the customer the blade is missing, or I'll just hide it in my drawer. And if I absolutely can't get out of it, I'm just shaking through the entire shave. It's getting really hard to do my job.
When you're not at work, do you still find yourself feeling anxious or fearful about the straight razor, or is it only when you're at work or thinking about using it for a shave?

It's mostly just at work, or when it's right in front of me. I mean... I know it’s just a tool I trained with, and I can use clippers all day long without a second thought. But when that straight razor is just sitting there open at my station, it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, or... or cut myself badly. So it really hits me when it's right there.
Outside of the situation with the straight razor at work, do you find yourself avoiding or feeling anxious about other things in your daily life?

No, not really. It's just the razor. I don't have any problems with anything else, like driving or being in crowds or anything like that. My life outside of work is pretty normal, honestly. It's just... this one specific thing that's completely messing up my job.
When you’re at work and you see the straight razor or think about having to use it, do you ever experience symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or a feeling like you can’t breathe?

Yeah, I do. The second I hear a client ask for a razor shave, or... or if I just see the blade flipped open, it happens. My chest tightens up right away, and my hands get really sweaty. It’s like my body just wants to physically back away from it before I even have a chance to think.
Has this kind of physical anxiety reaction—like chest tightness or sweating—ever happened to you outside of work or away from the straight razor?

No, never. It's really just when I'm dealing with the razor. I don't get that tight chest or the sweating any other time. If I'm not at the shop or looking at that blade, I feel completely fine physically.
Do you ever feel anxious or have those physical symptoms even when you're just thinking about using the straight razor later in the day, like when you're preparing for work or seeing it in your bag?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get the sweating or the tight chest just getting ready for work in the morning. I might dread it a little, knowing I have to go in and deal with it, but the physical reaction... that really only hits me when I'm actually at the shop and faced with the razor.
How long have you been feeling this way about the straight razor? Has it been going on for at least six months?

Yeah, it's definitely been longer than six months. I'd say it's been going on for about 11 months now. That's when the shop owner started pushing this new straight-razor shave package, and we started arguing about it. Ever since then, the physical reaction has just been there.
